modules.title: Responsible AI
modules.summary: Build a foundation in responsible AI principles and practical controls for safe, transparent, and accountable AI solutions.

tr.title: Sorumlu yapay zekâ
tr.summary: Güvenli, şeffaf ve hesap verebilir AI çözümleri için sorumlu yapay zekâ ilkeleri ve pratik denetimler konusunda temel oluşturun.

lessons.title: Principles of responsible AI
lessons.summary: Learn the six responsible AI principles and how they guide trustworthy AI solution design.
learningObjectives: Describe fairness, reliability, privacy, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability in AI
Identify responsible AI risks that accuracy alone does not address
Recognize why evaluation, documentation, and oversight support trustworthy AI
lessons.explanation:
Responsible AI is an approach for designing, building, and operating AI systems in ways that are safe, ethical, and trustworthy. A model is not ready just because it can produce accurate predictions. Teams also need to ask who might be affected, what data is used, how errors are found, and who owns the outcome.

Microsoft describes six core principles: **fairness**, **reliability and safety**, **privacy and security**, **inclusiveness**, **transparency**, and **accountability**. Fairness checks whether similar people or groups receive consistent treatment. Reliability and safety means dependable behavior and safe failure. Privacy and security protects data, identities, networks, and access. Inclusiveness considers people with different abilities, languages, contexts, and needs. Transparency helps stakeholders understand purpose, limits, and important behavior. Accountability keeps people and processes responsible for decisions and incidents.

These principles overlap. A loan assistance tool might compare error rates by applicant cohort, restrict access to sensitive data, document model limitations, require human review, and log deployment approvals.

terminology.definition: Developing and operating AI systems safely, ethically, and with trust.
Assessing whether similar people or groups are treated consistently.
Making purpose, limits, and behavior understandable.
Keeping people and processes responsible for outcomes.

lessons.businessScenario: Contoso is building an AI tool that prioritizes support requests and must show it does not systematically disadvantage a customer group.
lessons.technicalExample: The team evaluates errors by segment, restricts data access, documents limits, and stores approval records.

misconception.myth: Responsible AI is a final checklist after the model is accurate.
misconception.reality: Responsible AI is designed into the whole lifecycle: data choices, evaluation, documentation, access, monitoring, escalation, and human ownership.

lessons.examTakeaway: When a scenario mentions unequal outcomes, unsafe behavior, sensitive data, inaccessible design, unclear explanations, or missing ownership, map the clue to the matching responsible AI principle rather than to a model feature.
lessons.recap: Responsible AI uses fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability to make AI systems trustworthy in context.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Responsible AI is like opening a public playground: the equipment may work, but you still need safe surfaces, clear signs, access for different children, privacy rules, and an adult responsible for problems.
lessons.anotherExample: Woodgrove Bank adds an AI recommendation to route customer requests. It checks error rates for different customer groups, explains when staff should override a suggestion, and records who approved the release.

columns.title: Fairness / inclusiveness
points: Who might receive worse outcomes?
Can people with different abilities, languages, or contexts use the solution?

columns.title: Reliability / privacy
points: How does the system fail safely?
Which data, identities, and access paths need protection?

columns.title: Transparency / accountability
points: Can users understand purpose and limits?
Who reviews, approves, monitors, and responds to incidents?

data.title: Principle spotting
data.instructions: Read each clue and name the responsible AI principle it most directly suggests.

items.prompt: A hiring model has higher false negatives for one candidate group.
items.answer: Fairness: investigate and reduce unjustified outcome gaps.

items.prompt: Users cannot tell when a support reply was generated by AI.
items.answer: Transparency: disclose AI use and explain limitations.

items.prompt: No team owns incident response for model failures.
items.answer: Accountability: assign owners, approvals, monitoring, and escalation.

flashcards.back: Look for unjustified differences in outcomes for similar people or groups.
Look for dependable behavior, testing, safe failure, and monitoring under expected conditions.
Look for protecting data, identities, network paths, keys, and access permissions.
Look for explaining purpose, limitations, data use, and when AI is involved.
Look for a human owner, approval process, audit trail, and incident response.

A.explanation: Fairness, gruplar arasında adil muameleyi ve sonuç değerlendirmesini kapsar.

knowledgeCheck.stem: Privacy and security considerations apply only after an AI model is deployed to production.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Privacy and security should be considered across data collection, training, deployment, access control, monitoring, and retirement.

options.explanation: Choosing True misses that privacy and security risks must be addressed during data collection, training, deployment, monitoring, and retirement.
Correct. Responsible AI work applies privacy and security controls throughout the lifecycle, not only after production deployment.

tr.explanation: Privacy and security; veri toplama, eğitim, dağıtım, erişim denetimi, izleme ve kullanımdan kaldırma dahil tüm yaşam döngüsünde ele alınmalıdır.

FALSE.explanation: Doğru. Sorumlu yapay zekâ çalışmaları privacy ve security denetimlerini yalnızca üretimden sonra değil, tüm yaşam döngüsü boyunca uygular.

knowledgeCheck.stem: A model card states where the model performs poorly and which data was used for evaluation. Which responsible AI principle does this documentation most directly support?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Documentation that helps people understand model behavior, limitations, and evaluation evidence directly supports transparency.

options.explanation: It makes system behavior, limits, and evidence easier to inspect.
Inclusiveness is about designing for diverse users; documentation can help but is not primary here.
The statement does not focus on protecting data or access.
Reliability testing may be documented, but explaining limits is transparency.

tr.stem: Bir model kartı, modelin nerelerde zayıf performans gösterdiğini ve değerlendirmede hangi verilerin kullanıldığını belirtir. Bu belge doğrudan en çok hangi sorumlu yapay zekâ ilkesini destekler?
tr.explanation: İnsanların model davranışını, sınırlamalarını ve değerlendirme kanıtlarını anlamasına yardımcı olan belgeler doğrudan transparency ilkesini destekler.

A.explanation: Sistem davranışını, sınırlarını ve kanıtları incelemeyi kolaylaştırır.

B.explanation: Inclusiveness farklı kullanıcılar için tasarımla ilgilidir; belge yardımcı olabilir ama buradaki ana ilke değildir.

C.explanation: İfade veriyi veya erişimi korumaya odaklanmıyor.

D.explanation: Güvenilirlik testleri belgelenebilir; ancak sınırları açıklama eylemi transparency kapsamındadır.

knowledgeCheck.stem: Which **two** practices best support accountability for an AI solution?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Accountability is strengthened by traceable ownership and operational monitoring so people can govern changes and respond to issues.

options.text: Record who approved each model deployment and why.
options.explanation: Change records create ownership and traceability.

options.text: Monitor production behavior and alert owners when drift or incidents occur.
options.explanation: Monitoring and alerts help accountable owners respond.

options.text: Remove all human review so the model is the final decision maker.
options.explanation: Accountability requires meaningful human oversight, especially for impactful decisions.

options.text: Hide evaluation results to avoid confusing users.
options.explanation: Hiding evidence undermines transparency and accountability.

tr.stem: Bir yapay zekâ çözümünde accountability ilkesini en iyi destekleyen **iki** uygulama hangisidir?
tr.explanation: Accountability; değişiklikleri yönetmek ve sorunlara yanıt vermek için izlenebilir sahiplik ve operasyonel izleme ile güçlenir.

A.text: Her model dağıtımını kimin ve neden onayladığını kaydetmek.
A.explanation: Değişiklik kayıtları sahiplik ve izlenebilirlik sağlar.

B.text: Üretim davranışını izlemek ve sapma ya da olay olduğunda sahipleri uyarmak.
B.explanation: İzleme ve uyarılar sorumlu sahiplerin yanıt vermesine yardım eder.

C.text: Tüm insan incelemesini kaldırıp modeli nihai karar verici yapmak.
C.explanation: Accountability, özellikle etkili kararlarda anlamlı insan gözetimi gerektirir.

D.text: Kullanıcıların kafası karışmasın diye değerlendirme sonuçlarını gizlemek.
D.explanation: Kanıtları gizlemek transparency ve accountability ilkelerini zayıflatır.

tr.title: Sorumlu yapay zekâ ilkeleri
tr.summary: Sorumlu yapay zekânın altı temel ilkesini ve AI senaryolarında nasıl kullanıldığını öğrenin.
learningObjectives: AI için fairness, reliability, privacy, inclusiveness, transparency ve accountability ilkelerini açıkla
Doğruluğun tek başına çözmediği responsible AI risklerini belirle
Değerlendirme, dokümantasyon ve gözetimin güvenilir AI çözümlerini nasıl desteklediğini tanı
tr.explanation: Bu ders, AI-901 kapsamındaki kavramları özgün örneklerle açıklar. Sorumlu yapay zekâ; fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency ve accountability ilkelerini birlikte uygular. Üretken AI senaryolarında system message, evaluation, grounding, human oversight ve monitoring gibi katmanlar tek bir ayardan daha güvenilir sonuç verir.

terminology.definition: AI sistemlerini güvenli, etik ve güvenilir şekilde geliştirme yaklaşımı.
Model davranışını kalite, güvenlik ve uygunluk açısından ölçme süreci.

tr.businessScenario: Contoso, AI destekli bir asistanı yayınlamadan önce sınırlarını, kaynaklarını ve insan gözetimini tanımlar.
tr.technicalExample: Ekip system message yazar, test istemleri çalıştırır, kaynak belgelerle grounding kullanır ve olayları izlemek için sahipler atar.

misconception.myth: Sorumlu yapay zekâ, model doğru çalıştıktan sonra yapılan son kontroldür.
misconception.reality: Sorumlu yapay zekâ; veri seçimi, değerlendirme, dokümantasyon, erişim, izleme, eskalasyon ve insan sahipliği dahil tüm yaşam döngüsüne tasarlanır.

tr.examTakeaway: Senaryoda eşit olmayan sonuçlar, güvenli olmayan davranış, hassas veri, erişilebilir olmayan tasarım, belirsiz açıklamalar veya sahiplik eksikliği geçiyorsa ipucunu bir model özelliğine değil ilgili responsible AI ilkesine eşleyin.
tr.recap: Responsible AI; fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency ve accountability ilkelerini kullanarak AI sistemlerini bağlam içinde güvenilir kılar.
tr.simplerExplanation: Responsible AI, halka açık bir oyun alanı açmaya benzer: ekipman çalışabilir; ama güvenli zemin, net tabelalar, farklı çocuklara erişim, gizlilik kuralları ve sorunlardan sorumlu bir yetişkin gerekir.
tr.anotherExample: Woodgrove Bank, müşteri taleplerini yönlendirmek için bir AI önerisi ekler. Farklı müşteri grupları için hata oranlarını kontrol eder, personelin öneriyi ne zaman geçersiz kılacağını açıklar ve yayını kimin onayladığını kaydeder.

lessons.title: Applying responsible AI: safety, transparency, and oversight
lessons.summary: Turn responsible AI principles into practical controls such as system messages, evaluation, grounding, monitoring, and human oversight.
learningObjectives: Identify controls that turn responsible AI principles into product practices
Explain how system messages, grounding, and evaluation reduce generative AI risk
Choose monitoring or human review for sensitive or uncertain AI outputs
lessons.explanation:
Responsible AI becomes real when principles are built into the product lifecycle. A team starts by defining purpose, users, data, and possible harms. Then it chooses controls for data preparation, prompting, model selection, deployment, user experience, and monitoring.

For generative AI, a **system message** is an important control. It gives high-priority instructions about role, scope, tone, boundaries, refusal behavior, and tool use. But a system message is only one layer. Teams should create test sets with normal and adversarial prompts, evaluate whether the model follows boundaries, use grounding when answers must come from approved sources, and add content safety or human review where risk is higher.

Transparency means users know what the feature is for, what it cannot do, and when to seek help. Oversight means a model is not treated as the final authority for impactful decisions. Accountability means owners are named, changes are logged, production behavior is monitored, and incidents have a response path.

terminology.definition: High-priority instructions and context that steer a chat model.
Providing trusted source content so a generative response is based on that content.
People review, approve, or intervene in AI-assisted decisions.
Testing model behavior for quality, safety, fairness, and fit.

lessons.businessScenario: Fabrikam is preparing an HR policy assistant that should answer from approved documents and route uncertain cases to HR staff.
lessons.technicalExample: Developers write a system message, connect approved documents through retrieval, run a prompt test set, and assign review owners.

misconception.myth: A safety message alone makes a generative AI assistant safe enough for customers.
misconception.reality: Safety instructions help, but teams also need grounded sources, content filters, evaluations, monitoring, escalation paths, and human review for sensitive outcomes.

lessons.examTakeaway: For implementation scenarios, choose layered controls: define allowed behavior, ground answers in approved content, evaluate outputs, monitor use, and keep humans in the loop when impact or uncertainty is high.
lessons.recap: Applying responsible AI turns principles into controls such as safety instructions, data protection, evaluation, grounded responses, monitoring, documentation, and human oversight.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Think of a customer assistant like a new employee. A handbook helps, but you also give approved references, limit what they can do, review risky answers, and watch for patterns that need coaching.
lessons.anotherExample: Proseware builds an HR benefits assistant. It answers from approved policy pages, refuses medical advice, logs low-confidence questions, and routes exceptions to an HR specialist.

data.title: Responsible AI control loop
data.caption: The loop starts with allowed use, grounds the assistant in approved content, evaluates outputs, monitors real use, escalates sensitive cases, and feeds improvements back into the instructions.

data.title: Layer controls, not promises
data.body: A safety system message is useful, but it is not a substitute for evaluation, grounding, access control, content safety, logging, and human review when answers affect people.

flashcards.back: Instructions that define the assistant's role, boundaries, refusal behavior, and tone.
A response based on approved source content rather than only the model's general knowledge.
Representative prompts and expected behaviors used to test quality and safety before release.
A person reviews or approves outputs when impact, uncertainty, or sensitivity is high.
Logs, feedback, or metrics that reveal unsafe outputs, drift, or gaps after deployment.

knowledgeCheck.scenario: Woodgrove Bank plans a loan assistance tool. The tool drafts recommendations for loan officers, but final decisions remain with trained staff. The team found higher error rates for applicants with limited credit histories.

statements.text: Review error rates by relevant cohorts before expanding the pilot.
statements.explanation: Cohort analysis helps detect fairness and reliability problems.

statements.text: Keep the issue private from loan officers because the model will improve over time.
statements.explanation: Operational users need clear limits and escalation guidance.

statements.text: Require staff to document when they override a model recommendation.
statements.explanation: Override records support accountability and improvement.

statements.text: Use more applicant data than necessary because more data always improves safety.
statements.explanation: Privacy requires minimizing and protecting sensitive data.

tr.explanation: Sorumlu yapay zekâ eylemleri fairness testi, insan gözetimi, transparency ve hassas verinin güvenli işlenmesini birleştirir.

statements.s2: Model zamanla iyileşeceği için sorunu kredi uzmanlarından gizleyin.

explanations.s3: Geçersiz kılma kayıtları accountability ve iyileştirmeyi destekler.

knowledgeCheck.stem: A safety system message can help guide model behavior, but it should be used with other controls such as evaluation, grounding, and content safety.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: System messages are useful guardrails, but responsible deployment needs layered controls and ongoing measurement.

options.explanation: Correct. A safety system message can steer behavior, but evaluation, grounding, content safety, and monitoring provide needed additional controls.
Choosing False misses that system messages are useful guardrails when they are combined with other responsible deployment controls.

tr.stem: Bir safety system message model davranışını yönlendirmeye yardımcı olabilir; ancak evaluation, grounding ve content safety gibi diğer denetimlerle birlikte kullanılmalıdır.
tr.explanation: System message yararlı bir koruma katmanıdır; ancak sorumlu dağıtım katmanlı denetimler ve sürekli ölçüm gerektirir.

TRUE.explanation: Doğru. Safety system message davranışı yönlendirebilir; ancak evaluation, grounding, content safety ve izleme gibi ek denetimler de gerekir.

FALSE.explanation: False seçeneği, system message yönergelerinin diğer sorumlu dağıtım denetimleriyle birlikte kullanıldığında yararlı olduğunu gözden kaçırır.

knowledgeCheck.stem: What should the team do before allowing the assistant to answer customers?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Testing benign and adversarial prompts against the defined scope helps validate that the assistant follows boundaries and escalates appropriately.

options.text: Create a test set that includes normal support questions and boundary cases.
options.explanation: A test set validates behavior across expected and risky inputs.

options.text: Remove the system message so the model can be more creative.
options.explanation: Removing instructions weakens consistency and safety.

options.text: Tell customers the assistant is always correct.
options.explanation: Responsible AI avoids overclaiming and should communicate limitations.

options.text: Skip human review because the model uses a large training set.

learningObjectives: Responsible AI ilkelerini ürün uygulamalarına dönüştüren kontrolleri belirle

tr.explanation: Bu ders, AI-901 kapsamındaki kavramları özgün örneklerle açıklar. Sorumlu yapay zekâ; fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency ve accountability ilkelerini birlikte uygular. lessons.title: Common AI workloads
lessons.summary: Identify common AI workloads such as generative and agentic AI, text analysis, speech, computer vision, and information extraction.
learningObjectives: Identify generative, agentic, text, speech, vision, and extraction workloads
Match input types and business goals to the right AI workload
Distinguish analysis workloads from content generation and tool-using agents
lessons.explanation:
AI workloads are categories of tasks that AI systems perform. For AI-901, recognize the scenario from the input, output, and goal.

**Generative AI** creates new content such as text, code, images, or summaries from prompts. **Agentic AI** uses a model with instructions and tools so it can plan steps or take actions within boundaries. **Text analysis** finds meaning in text: key phrases, named entities, sentiment, language, or summaries. **Speech** workloads convert speech to text, text to speech, translate spoken language, or support voice interactions. **Computer vision** analyzes images or video, such as detecting objects or extracting visible text. **Information extraction** turns unstructured content such as documents, images, audio, or video into structured fields that business processes can use.

Choose the workload by asking: What is the source content? What output is needed? Audio to captions is speech recognition. Scanned form to fields is information extraction. Comments to sentiment and entities is text analysis.

terminology.definition: NLP techniques that identify meaning, entities, sentiment, key phrases, or summaries.
Converting spoken audio into text.
Analyzing images or video to detect visual features or extract text.
Transforming unstructured content into structured values.

lessons.businessScenario: Tailwind Traders wants to summarize reviews, caption videos, read receipt photos, and generate campaign images.
lessons.technicalExample: A solution can combine Azure Language, Azure Speech, Azure Vision or Content Understanding, and a generative model.

misconception.myth: All AI workloads are basically the same if they use a model.
misconception.reality: Workloads differ by input type, output type, and task.

lessons.examTakeaway: Identify the workload from verbs such as summarize, transcribe, synthesize, detect, classify, extract, or generate.
lessons.recap: Common AI workloads include text, speech, vision, generation, agents, and extraction.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Think of workloads as specialist departments: one reads text, one listens, one looks at images, one extracts fields, and one creates new content.
lessons.anotherExample: A call center may use speech recognition to transcribe calls, text analysis to detect sentiment, and summarization to produce notes.

lessons.title: Models, training, and inference
lessons.summary: Understand model components, training, evaluation, deployment, and inference at a beginner-friendly level.
learningObjectives: Distinguish training, evaluation, deployment, and inference in an AI lifecycle
Identify how model capabilities and configuration affect solution fit
Explain why deployed model endpoints are tested before business use
lessons.explanation:
An AI model maps inputs to outputs. In traditional machine learning, training uses data and an algorithm to adjust model parameters. In generative AI, large pretrained models have already learned broad patterns, and you often select, configure, ground, or fine-tune a model rather than train one from the beginning.

**Training** is the learning phase. **Evaluation** checks whether the model is good enough for the intended task and whether risks are acceptable. **Deployment** makes a chosen model available for applications to call. **Inference** happens when new input is sent to the deployed model and the model returns a prediction, classification, generated response, or other output.

Model choice depends on capability. A text-only model is not suitable if the application must reason over photos. A multimodal model may be needed for image plus text prompts. A speech model is appropriate for transcription or synthesis. Deployment choices and parameters also matter, and supported settings can differ by model and API.

terminology.definition: A system that maps inputs to outputs based on learned patterns or configured capabilities.
The process of adjusting a model by learning from data.
Using a trained or deployed model to produce output for new input.
Making a selected model available for applications to call.

lessons.businessScenario: Adventure Works needs to choose between a text model for policy questions, a multimodal model for equipment photos, and a speech model for voice calls.
lessons.technicalExample: A developer deploys a model, sends a chat request with system and user messages, reviews token usage, and evaluates responses.

misconception.myth: After a model is deployed, it no longer needs evaluation or monitoring.
misconception.reality: Deployment enables inference, but teams still evaluate, monitor, and update controls as usage changes.

lessons.examTakeaway: Know the lifecycle words: training learns patterns, deployment exposes the model, and inference uses it for new inputs.
lessons.recap: Models are chosen by capability and then evaluated for the scenario. Deployment and inference are how applications use them.
lessons.simplerExplanation: Training is like studying examples; inference is answering a new question after studying; deployment is making the helper available.
lessons.anotherExample: A sentiment classifier trained on product reviews may not work well on medical notes unless evaluated for that context.

lessons.title: Generative AI models and their configuration
lessons.summary: Learn how prompts, messages, tokens, temperature, grounding, and deployment settings influence generative AI behavior.
learningObjectives: Identify prompts, system messages, tokens, temperature, grounding, and deployments
Explain how configuration choices influence consistency, creativity, and safety
Choose grounding and low temperature when answers must follow approved sources
lessons.explanation:
Generative AI models produce new content from input. In chat-style applications, the input is usually a sequence of messages. A **system message** gives high-priority instructions such as role, scope, tone, and boundaries. A **user message** contains the user's request. Previous assistant messages can provide context or examples.

Models process text as **tokens**, which are chunks of text rather than always whole words. Token usage affects how much context fits in a request. Many chat APIs also let you set a maximum output token value so responses do not run longer than intended.

Some model/API combinations support parameters such as **temperature**. Lower temperature generally makes output more focused and repeatable; higher temperature can make output more varied. Newer reasoning models can support different parameter sets, so verify what the chosen model accepts.

**Grounding** provides retrieved or trusted content to the model. RAG retrieves relevant passages from an index, adds them to the prompt, and asks the model to answer from that content. Grounding can improve usefulness and citations, but does not guarantee correctness.

terminology.definition: Input instructions or content provided to a generative model.
High-priority chat instructions that guide behavior.
A chunk of text processed by a language model.
A generation parameter, when supported, that influences randomness.
Supplying trusted or retrieved content to reduce unsupported answers.

lessons.businessScenario: Fabrikam wants a consistent benefits FAQ grounded in HR documents and a marketing brainstormer that may produce varied ideas.
lessons.technicalExample: The FAQ assistant uses strict system instructions, RAG over approved HR pages, and low temperature when supported.

misconception.myth: Grounding guarantees that every answer is correct.
misconception.reality: Grounding can reduce unsupported answers, but poor retrieval or unclear instructions can still produce wrong or incomplete responses.

lessons.examTakeaway: Connect the setting to the goal: low variation for repeatability, grounding for source-based answers, and system messages for boundaries.
lessons.recap: Generative AI behavior is shaped by messages, tokens, parameters, grounding, and deployment choices.
lessons.simplerExplanation: The system message is the assignment brief, grounding is the source packet, tokens are the space available, and temperature is how adventurous the draft should be.
lessons.anotherExample: A policy helper should answer from approved documents and cite sources; an ideation tool may allow more variety after review.
